checks.name: a5-crash-resume-digest-binding
checks.summary: Case A (crash before provider result journaled): FindPendingProviderResult finds nothing; the resumed Execution re-runs the provider exactly once (FakeInvocationRunner.CallCount()==1). Case B digest match (crash after journaling, Work Packet unchanged): the recovered record's WorkPacketDigest equals the new attempt's own digest; the recovered raw payload re-passes provider.CodexAdapter.Parse; a fresh FakeInvocationRunner records zero calls (adoption, not re-run). Case B digest mismatch (Work Packet content changed between attempts): digests differ; the resumed Execution re-runs the provider exactly once. In every case: attempt2.claim.ExecutionID != attempt1.claim.ExecutionID, attempt2.claim.FencingToken > attempt1.claim.FencingToken (strict), the crashed attempt's own late AcceptResult (its original lease/version/fencing token) is rejected with domain.ErrLeaseExpired (errors.Is confirmed), and a domain.Execution snapshot of the resumed Execution taken immediately before and immediately after that rejected call is unchanged (direct store.Transact/u.Execution comparison, not inference).

checks.name: a6-real-sigkill-durability
checks.summary: Parent re-executes os.Args[0] with -test.run=^TestHelperProcessJournalAppendAndBlock$ and env var AGENTIC_LOOP_RUNNER_CRASH_HELPER=1 plus AGENTIC_LOOP_RUNNER_CRASH_DIR=<t.TempDir()>. The child opens a real runner.Journal in that directory, Appends (fsyncs) one event, writes a marker file, then blocks in select{}. The parent polls only for that marker file with a 15s bounded deadline (no fixed sleep), then syscall.Kill(-pid, SIGKILL)s the whole process group, confirms cmd.Wait() returns a non-nil error within a further bounded 15s deadline, then OpenJournal on the same directory from a fresh *Journal and replays exactly the one fsync'd event. Deterministic on GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest: no privilege, no namespace, no container; the only synchronisation is the marker-file poll.

checks.name: a13-lease-keeper
checks.summary: TestLeaseKeeperRenewsAndHeartbeatsAsDistinctOperations: 4 explicit ticks of 20s each over an injected mutableClock (80s total, > the 1-minute LeaseTTL) each issue a distinct Renew and a distinct Heartbeat request id (RequestBase:renew-N / RequestBase:heartbeat-N); every RenewResponse.ExpiresAt strictly advances, proving each is a genuine renewal rather than an idempotent replay. TestLeaseKeeperRefusesRenewUnderStaleFencingToken: a mismatched fencing token bubbles domain.ErrStaleFence unmodified. TestLeaseKeeperStopsRenewingOnceLeaseIsExpiredWithoutResurrectingIt: after the clock is advanced past the TTL with no renewal, the first Tick returns domain.ErrLeaseExpired and out.Expired=true; a second Tick issues no further Renew call (out.Renewed=false) while still heartbeating.

checks.name: a4-and-a12-journey-one
checks.summary: One self-contained test function, own t.TempDir() fixtures, own context deadline, injected mutableClock and journeyIDs generator, no sleep, no goroutine timer. Drives: enrollment issue -> Begin -> Complete -> VerifySession (runner id used as claim caller) -> Capture -> Plan -> Prepare -> Claim -> Workspace.Create -> Start -> 4 LeaseKeeper ticks spanning > 1 LeaseTTL -> process Permit -> Work Packet build+Validate -> FakeInvocationRunner via ProviderClient (real provider.CodexAdapter.Build/Parse) -> Checkpoint -> result Permit -> AcceptResult. Terminal status asserted == domain.ExecutionSucceeded, checkpoint == 'checkpoint-journey-1', and the Increment Artifact digest (provider.Result.OutputDigest, exposed as ProviderResult.Output) is non-empty. A12 workspace confinement asserted in the same test: Invocation.WorkingDirectory equals the symlink-resolved workspace path, no argv element resolves outside the workspace root, Invocation.Environment is empty (no grant merged in this journey), the workspace is not a symlink and is not group/world accessible (perm & 0077 == 0), and Workspace.Path rejects a '../escape-attempt' path.
